prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: waiting for the loss adjuster. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a loss adjuster is clearly needed, I book the appointment as early as possible and tell the member to expect a wait, because the delay is usually shorter when everyone knows the next step straight away."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the case is still within delegated authority but I am waiting for a loss adjuster’s report, I keep the file open with a clear diary date and do not leave the member guessing about progress."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I am waiting for the adjuster, I prefer to gather the photos, receipts and policy details first, because a complete pack reduces avoidable back-and-forth later."},{"type":"observation","content":"When storm damage or escape of water is obvious from the evidence, I can often set expectations on likely liability before the adjuster attends, even if final settlement still depends on their visit."},{"type":"fact","content":"When access is difficult, I note that the loss adjuster may be delayed and I ask the member to keep any temporary repairs in place unless they are unsafe, so the visit still has something to assess."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the loss adjuster is handling a high-volume event, a short, plain update from me every few days helps more than a long explanation, because members mainly want reassurance that the case has not stalled."},{"type":"preference","content":"When waiting is likely to run beyond a week, I prefer to explain why the adjuster is needed and what they will look for, because members cope better when the process feels purposeful rather than bureaucratic."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there is a risk of worsening damage, I do not wait passively for the adjuster if emergency mitigation is needed; I authorise reasonable immediate steps and then let the adjuster review the outcome."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the adjuster’s report is the last missing item, I avoid re-asking for the same documents from the member, because duplicate chasers create the impression that nothing is moving."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the case is nearly ready for settlement after the adjuster visit, I like to prepare the draft decision in advance, so I can move quickly once the report lands."}]}
